**Bitcoin** (abbreviation: **BTC**; [sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency_symbol "Currency symbol"): **₿**) is the first [decentralized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralization "Decentralization")[cryptocurrency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency "Cryptocurrency"). Based on a [free-market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free-market "Free-market") ideology, bitcoin was invented in 2008 when an unknown person published a [white paper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_paper "White paper") under the pseudonym of [Satoshi Nakamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satoshi_Nakamoto "Satoshi Nakamoto").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-whoissn-6) Use of bitcoin as a currency began in 2009,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-NY2011-7) with the release of its [open-source implementation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software "Open-source software").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 1 From 2021 to 2025, [El Salvador adopted it](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_in_El_Salvador "Bitcoin in El Salvador") as [legal tender currency before revoking it](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_Law "Bitcoin Law").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-BTCSVSept7FT-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-El_Salvador_Abandons_Bitcoin_as_Legal_Tender-10)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Bitcoin_is_no_longer_legal_tender_in_El_Salvador-11) As bitcoin is [pseudonymous](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pseudonym "wikt:pseudonym"), [its use by criminals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency_and_crime "Cryptocurrency and crime") has attracted the attention of regulators, leading to [its ban by several countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legality_of_cryptocurrency_by_country_or_territory "Legality of cryptocurrency by country or territory").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-SunYin2019-12)

Bitcoin works through the collaboration of computers, each of which acts as a [node](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Node_(networking) "Node (networking)") in the [peer-to-peer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-to-peer "Peer-to-peer")[bitcoin network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_network "Bitcoin network"). Each node maintains an independent copy of a public [distributed ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distributed_ledger "Distributed ledger") of [transactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transaction_processing "Transaction processing"), called a [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain"), without [central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centralisation "Centralisation")[oversight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_(social_and_political) "Power (social and political)"). Transactions are validated through the use of [cryptography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptography "Cryptography"), preventing one person from [spending another person's bitcoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theft "Theft"), as long as the owner of the bitcoin keeps certain sensitive data secret.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 5

[Consensus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consensus_(computer_science) "Consensus (computer science)") between nodes about the content of the blockchain is achieved using a [computationally intensive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_complexity "Computational complexity") process based on [proof of work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_of_work "Proof of work"), called [mining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_mining "Bitcoin mining"), which is performed by [purpose-built computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application-specific_integrated_circuit "Application-specific integrated circuit").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 12 Mining consumes large quantities of electricity, with surveyed miners reporting that 52% of their electricity use came from [sustainable energy sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sustainable_energy "Sustainable energy"), and has been criticized for [its environmental impact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_impact_of_bitcoin "Environmental impact of bitcoin").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-nytimes_20210903-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-14)

## History

### Background

Before bitcoin, several [digital cash technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_cash "Digital cash") were released, starting with [David Chaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Chaum "David Chaum")'s [ecash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecash "Ecash") in the 1980s.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Narayanan2017-15) The idea that solutions to computational puzzles could have some value was first proposed by cryptographers [Cynthia Dwork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cynthia_Dwork "Cynthia Dwork") and [Moni Naor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moni_Naor "Moni Naor") in 1992.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-16)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Narayanan2017-15) The concept was [independently rediscovered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_discovery "Multiple discovery") by [Adam Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Back "Adam Back") who developed [Hashcash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashcash "Hashcash"), a [proof-of-work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof-of-work "Proof-of-work") scheme for [spam control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-spam_techniques "Anti-spam techniques") in 1997.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Narayanan2017-15) The first proposals for distributed digital scarcity-based [cryptocurrencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrencies "Cryptocurrencies") came from [cypherpunks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cypherpunk "Cypherpunk")[Wei Dai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wei_Dai "Wei Dai") (b-money) and [Nick Szabo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Szabo "Nick Szabo") ([bit gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bit_gold "Bit gold")) in 1998.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-17) In 2004, [Hal Finney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hal_Finney_(cypherpunk) "Hal Finney (cypherpunk)") developed the first currency based on reusable proof of work.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-18) These various attempts were not successful:[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Narayanan2017-15) Chaum's concept required centralized control and no banks wanted to sign on, Hashcash had no protection against [double-spending](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-spending "Double-spending"), while b-money and bit gold were not resistant to [Sybil attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sybil_attack "Sybil attack").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Narayanan2017-15)

### 2008–2009: Creation

| --- |
| [![Image 2: image icon](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/61/Searchtool.svg/20px-Searchtool.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Searchtool.svg)[Cover page of _The Times_ 3 January 2009 showing the headline used in the genesis block](https://www.thetimes03jan2009.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/genesis-block-newspaper-bitcoin.jpg) |

The domain name _bitcoin.org_ was registered on 18 August 2008.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-businessinsider_20171202-19) On 31 October 2008, a link to a [white paper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_paper "White paper") authored by [Satoshi Nakamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satoshi_Nakamoto "Satoshi Nakamoto") titled _Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System_ was posted to a cryptography mailing list.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wired_20181031-20) Nakamoto's identity remains unknown.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-whoissn-6) According to computer scientist [Arvind Narayanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arvind_Narayanan "Arvind Narayanan"), all individual components of bitcoin originated in earlier academic literature.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Narayanan2017-15) Nakamoto's innovation was their complex interplay which resulted in the first decentralized, [Sybil resistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sybil_attack "Sybil attack"), [Byzantine fault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_fault "Byzantine fault") tolerant digital cash system, that would eventually be referred to as the first blockchain.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Narayanan2017-15)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-te20151031-21) Nakamoto's paper was not [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review "Peer review") and was initially ignored by academics, who argued that it could not work.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Narayanan2017-15)

Nakamoto released bitcoin as [open-source software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software "Open-source software").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Humayun-2018-22) On 3 January 2009, the bitcoin network was created when Nakamoto mined the starting block of the chain, known as the _[genesis block](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genesis\_(blockchain) "Genesis (blockchain)")_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Wired:RFB-23) Embedded in this block was the text "The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of [second bailout for banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_United_Kingdom_bank_rescue_package "2009 United Kingdom bank rescue package")", which is the date and headline of an issue of _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_ newspaper.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-NY2011-7) Nine days later, Hal Finney received the first bitcoin transaction: ten bitcoins from Nakamoto.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-nytimes_20140830-24) Wei Dai and Nick Szabo were also early supporters.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Wired:RFB-23) On 22 May 2010, the first known [commercial transaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_transaction "Financial transaction") using bitcoin occurred when programmer Laszlo Hanyecz bought two [Papa John's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papa_John's "Papa John's") pizzas for ₿10,000, in what would later be celebrated as "Bitcoin Pizza Day".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cbsnews_20190516-25) Satoshi tasked Finnish developer and early Bitcoin contributor [Martti Malmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martti_Malmi?action=edit&redlink=1 "Martti Malmi (page does not exist)")[[fi](https://fi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martti%20Malmi "fi:Martti Malmi")] with creating content for the bitcoin.org website.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wired_20240223-26)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-DominicFrisby2014-27)

### 2010–2012: Early growth

[Blockchain analysts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain#Blockchain_analysis "Blockchain") estimate that Nakamoto had mined about one million bitcoins[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-28) before he disappeared in 2010 and handed the network alert key and control of the [code repository](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_repository "Software repository") over to [Gavin Andresen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin_Andresen "Gavin Andresen"). Andresen later became lead developer at the [Bitcoin Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_Foundation "Bitcoin Foundation"),[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-technologyreview_20140815-29)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-techcrunch_20150921-30) an [organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bitcoin_organizations "List of bitcoin organizations") founded in September 2012 to promote bitcoin.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-newyorker_20130401-31)

After early "[proof-of-concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof-of-concept "Proof-of-concept")" transactions, the first major users of bitcoin were [black markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_market "Black market"), such as the [dark web](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_web "Dark web")[Silk Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk_Road_(marketplace) "Silk Road (marketplace)"). During its 30 months of existence, beginning in February 2011, Silk Road exclusively accepted bitcoins as payment, transacting ₿9.9 million, worth about $214 million.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-JEP-32):222

### 2013–2014: First regulatory actions

In March 2013, the US [Financial Crimes Enforcement Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Crimes_Enforcement_Network "Financial Crimes Enforcement Network") (FinCEN) established regulatory guidelines for "decentralized virtual currencies" such as bitcoin, classifying American bitcoin miners who sell their generated bitcoins as [money services businesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_services_business "Money services business"), subject to registration and other legal obligations.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-arstechnica_20130319-33) In May 2013, US authorities seized the unregistered [exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency_exchange "Cryptocurrency exchange")[Mt. Gox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mt._Gox "Mt. Gox").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-34) In June 2013, the US [Drug Enforcement Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_Enforcement_Administration "Drug Enforcement Administration") seized ₿11.02 from an individual attempting to use them to purchase illicit drugs. This marked the first time a government agency had seized bitcoins.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-35) The FBI seized about ₿30,000 in October 2013 from Silk Road, following the arrest of its founder [Ross Ulbricht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Ulbricht "Ross Ulbricht").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-36)

In December 2013, the [People's Bank of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Bank_of_China "People's Bank of China") prohibited Chinese financial institutions from using bitcoin.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bbc_25428866-37) After the announcement, the value of bitcoin dropped,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-smh_20131206-38) and [Baidu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baidu "Baidu") no longer accepted bitcoins for certain services.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloomberg_20131207-39) Buying real-world goods with any virtual currency had been illegal in China since at least 2009.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-mofcom_200906063642-40)

### 2015–2019

Research produced by the [University of Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cambridge "University of Cambridge") estimated that in 2017, there were 2.9 to 5.8 million unique users using a [cryptocurrency wallet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency_wallet "Cryptocurrency wallet"), most of them using bitcoin.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-41) In August 2017, the [SegWit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SegWit "SegWit") software upgrade was activated. Segwit was intended to support the [Lightning Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning_Network "Lightning Network") as well as improve [scalability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scalability "Scalability").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wsj_1500656084-42) SegWit opponents, who supported larger blocks as a scalability solution, [forked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fork_(blockchain) "Fork (blockchain)") to create [Bitcoin Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_Cash "Bitcoin Cash"), one of many [forks of bitcoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bitcoin_forks "List of bitcoin forks").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnn_20170801-43)

In December 2017, the first [futures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Futures_contract "Futures contract") on bitcoin was introduced by the [Chicago Mercantile Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Mercantile_Exchange "Chicago Mercantile Exchange") (CME).[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnbc_20171217-44)

In February 2018, the price crashed after China imposed a complete ban on bitcoin trading.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-marketwatch_20170209-45) The percentage of bitcoin trading in the Chinese [renminbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi") fell from over 90% in September 2017 to less than 1% in June 2018.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-xinhuanet_137308879-46) During the same year, bitcoin prices were negatively affected by several hacks or thefts from cryptocurrency exchanges.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-reuters_20180703-47)

### 2020–present

In 2020, some major companies and institutions started to acquire bitcoin: [MicroStrategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MicroStrategy "MicroStrategy") invested $250 million in bitcoin as a [treasury reserve asset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasury_management "Treasury management"),[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-independent_1919178-49)[Square, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square,_Inc. "Square, Inc."), $50 million,[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-50) and [MassMutual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MassMutual "MassMutual"), $100 million.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloomberg_20201211-51) In November 2020, [PayPal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PayPal "PayPal") added support for bitcoin in the US.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-techcrunch_20201113-52)

In February 2021, bitcoin's [market capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalization "Market capitalization") reached $1 trillion for the first time.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-53) In November 2021, the [Taproot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taproot_(fork) "Taproot (fork)")[soft-fork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft-fork "Soft-fork") upgrade was activated, adding support for [Schnorr signatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schnorr_signature "Schnorr signature"), improved functionality of [smart contracts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_contract "Smart contract") and [Lightning Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning_Network "Lightning Network").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnbc_20211114-54) Before, bitcoin only used a custom [elliptic curve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliptic_curve_cryptography "Elliptic curve cryptography") with the [ECDSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECDSA "ECDSA") algorithm to produce [signatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_signature "Digital signature").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-55):101 In September 2021, bitcoin became [legal tender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_tender "Legal tender") currency [in El Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_in_El_Salvador "Bitcoin in El Salvador"), alongside the US dollar.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-BTCSVSept7FT-9) In October 2021, the first bitcoin futures [exchange-traded fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exchange-traded_fund "Exchange-traded fund") (ETF), called BITO, from [ProShares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ProShares "ProShares") was approved by the [SEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission") and listed on the [CME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Mercantile_Exchange "Chicago Mercantile Exchange").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wsj_11634376601-56)

In early 2022, during the [Canadian trucker protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_convoy_protest "Canada convoy protest") opposing [COVID-19 vaccine mandates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine_misinformation_and_hesitancy "COVID-19 vaccine misinformation and hesitancy"), organizers turned to bitcoin to receive donations after traditional financial platforms restricted access to funding.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-57)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-theglobeandmail_20241208-58) Proponents highlighted bitcoin's use as a tool for fundraising in situations where access to conventional financial systems may be restricted.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-forbes_20240620-59)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-yahoo_200403223-60) In May and June 2022, the bitcoin price fell following the collapses of [TerraUSD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra_(blockchain) "Terra (blockchain)"), a [stablecoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stablecoin "Stablecoin"),[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnbc_20220510-61) and the [Celsius Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celsius_Network "Celsius Network"), a cryptocurrency loan company.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-theguardian_20220618_bitcoin-62)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-nytimes_20220613-63)

In 2023, ordinals—[non-fungible tokens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token "Non-fungible token") (NFTs)—on bitcoin, went live.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-64) As of June 2023, River Financial estimated that bitcoin had 81.7 million users, about 1% of the global population.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bbc_68434579-65)

### Units and divisibility

The [unit of account](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_of_account "Unit of account") of the bitcoin system is the _bitcoin_. It is most commonly represented with the [symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency_symbol "Currency symbol") ₿ designed in 2010[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-unicode-10-1) and the [currency code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency_code "Currency code") BTC. However, the BTC code does not conform to [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217 "ISO 4217") as BT is the country code of Bhutan,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-ssrn.3383734-73) and ISO 4217 requires the first letter used in global commodities to be 'X'.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-ssrn.3383734-73) XBT, a code that conforms to [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217 "ISO 4217") though not officially part of it,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-ssrn.3383734-73) is used by [Bloomberg L.P.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_L.P. "Bloomberg L.P.")[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-techcrunch_20130809-74)

No uniform [capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitalization "Capitalization") convention exists; some sources use _Bitcoin_, capitalized, to refer to the technology and [network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_network "Computer network"), and _bitcoin_, lowercase, for the unit of account.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-newyorker_20130401-31) The _[Cambridge Advanced Learner's Dictionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge\_Advanced\_Learner's\_Dictionary "Cambridge Advanced Learner's Dictionary")_ and the _[Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford\_Advanced\_Learner's\_Dictionary "Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary")_ use the capitalized and lowercase variants without distinction.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-75)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-archive_202205030922-76)

One bitcoin is divisible to eight decimal places.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 5 Units for smaller amounts of bitcoin are the millibitcoin (mBTC), equal to 1⁄1000 bitcoin, and the satoshi[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-satoshi-2) (sat), representing 1⁄100 000 000 (one hundred millionth) bitcoin, the smallest amount possible.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-satoshi_unit-3) 100,000 satoshis are one mBTC.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnn_20140709-77)

### Blockchain

As a [decentralized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralization "Decentralization") system, bitcoin operates without a central authority or single administrator,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Gervais2014-78) so that anyone can create a new bitcoin address and transact without needing any approval.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 1 This is accomplished through a specialized [distributed ledger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distributed_ledger "Distributed ledger") called a _[blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain")_ that records bitcoin transactions.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-econbc-79)

The blockchain is implemented as an ordered list of _blocks_. Each block contains the [hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic_hash_function "Cryptographic hash function") of the previous block, made by hashing its header twice with [SHA-256](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-256 "SHA-256"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-econbc-79) chaining them in chronological order.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 7[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-econbc-79) The blockchain is maintained by a [peer-to-peer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-to-peer "Peer-to-peer") network.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-JEP-32):215–219 Individual blocks, public addresses, and transactions within blocks are public information, and can be examined using a blockchain explorer.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-80)

Nodes validate and broadcast transactions. Each node maintains a copy of the blockchain for ownership verification.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-telegraph_10881213-81) A new block is created every 10 minutes on average, updating the blockchain across all nodes without central oversight. This process tracks bitcoin spending, ensuring each bitcoin is [spent only once](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-spending "Double-spending"). Unlike a traditional ledger that tracks physical currency, bitcoins exist digitally as [unspent outputs of transactions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unspent_outputs_of_transactions "Unspent outputs of transactions").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 5

### Addresses and transactions

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Bitcoin_Transaction_Visual.svg/250px-Bitcoin_Transaction_Visual.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bitcoin_Transaction_Visual.svg)

Simplified chain of ownership. In practice, a transaction can have more than one input and more than one output.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-EconOfBTC-82)

In the blockchain, bitcoins are linked to specific [strings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_(computer_science) "String (computer science)") called addresses. Most often, an address encodes a [hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash_(cryptography) "Hash (cryptography)") of a single [public key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_key "Public key"). Creating such an address involves generating a random private key and then computing the corresponding address. This process is almost instant, but the reverse (finding the private key for a given address) is nearly impossible.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 4 Publishing such a bitcoin address does not risk its private key, and it is extremely unlikely to accidentally generate a used key with funds. To use bitcoins, owners need their private key to [digitally sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_signature "Digital signature") transactions, which are verified by the network using the public key, keeping the private key secret.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 5 An address may encode the hash of a bitcoin script that specifies more complex requirements to spend the funds. One common example is "multisig", in which multiple distinct private keys must mutually sign any transaction that attempts to spend the funds.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 7

Bitcoin transactions use a [Forth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forth_(programming_language) "Forth (programming language)")-like [scripting language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scripting_language "Scripting language"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 5 involving one or more inputs and outputs. When sending bitcoins, a user specifies the recipients' addresses and the amount for each output. This allows sending bitcoins to several recipients in a single transaction. To prevent double-spending, each input must refer to a previous unspent output in the blockchain.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-EconOfBTC-82) Using multiple inputs is similar to using multiple coins in a cash transaction. As in a cash transaction, the sum of inputs can exceed the intended sum of payments. In such a case, an additional output can return the change back to the payer.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-EconOfBTC-82) Unallocated input satoshis in the transaction become the transaction fee.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-EconOfBTC-82)

Losing a private key means losing access to the bitcoins, with no other proof of ownership accepted by the [protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_protocol "Bitcoin protocol").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-JEP-32) For instance, in 2013, a user lost ₿7,500, valued at US$7.5 million, by accidentally discarding a [hard drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_disk_drive "Hard disk drive") with the private key.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cbslocal_20131129-83) It is estimated that around 20% of all bitcoins are lost.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wsj_1530798731-84) The private key must also be kept secret as its exposure, such as through a [data breach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_breach "Data breach"), can lead to theft of the associated bitcoins.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 10[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-theverge_5183356-85)As of December 2017, approximately ₿980,000 had been stolen from [cryptocurrency exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency_exchange "Cryptocurrency exchange").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-reuters_20171116-86)

### Mining

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Argo_Blockchain_Mirabel_Facility.jpg/250px-Argo_Blockchain_Mirabel_Facility.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Argo_Blockchain_Mirabel_Facility.jpg)

Bitcoin mining [facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center "Data center") with large amounts of mining hardware

Miners don't directly act as nodes, but do communicate with nodes. The mining process is primarily intended to prevent [double-spending](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-spending "Double-spending") and get all nodes to agree on the content of the blockchain, but it also has desirable side-effects such as making it infeasible for adversaries to stifle valid transactions or alter the historical record of transactions, since doing so generally requires the adversary to have access to more mining power than the rest of the network combined.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 12

The mining process in bitcoin involves maintaining the blockchain through computer [processing power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Processing_power "Processing power"). Miners group and broadcast new transactions into blocks, which are then verified by the network.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-econbc-79) Each block must contain a proof of work (PoW) to be accepted,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-econbc-79) involving finding a [nonce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic_nonce "Cryptographic nonce") number that, combined with the block content, produces a [hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic_hash "Cryptographic hash") numerically smaller than the network's _difficulty target_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 8 This PoW is simple to verify but hard to generate, requiring many attempts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 8 PoW forms the basis of bitcoin's [consensus mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consensus_(computer_science) "Consensus (computer science)").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Mingxiao2017-87)

The difficulty of generating a block is [deterministically adjusted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deterministic_algorithm "Deterministic algorithm") based on the [mining power on the network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashrate "Hashrate") by changing the difficulty target, which is recalibrated every 2,016 blocks (approximately two weeks) to maintain an average time of ten minutes between new blocks. The process requires significant computational power and specialized [hardware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_hardware "Computer hardware").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 8[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-taipeitimes_2003580449-88)

Miners who successfully create a new block with a valid nonce can collect transaction fees from the included transactions and a fixed reward in bitcoins.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloombergvance111413-89) To claim this reward, a special transaction called a _coinbase_ is included in the block, with the miner as the payee. All bitcoins in existence have been created through this type of transaction.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 8 This reward is halved every 210,000 blocks until ₿21 million[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-supply-5) have been issued in total, which is expected to occur around the year 2140. Afterward, miners will only earn from transaction fees. These fees are determined by the transaction's size and the amount of data stored, measured in satoshis per byte.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-qz_154877-90)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-EconOfBTC-82)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 8

The proof of work system and the chaining of blocks make blockchain modifications very difficult, as altering one block requires changing all subsequent blocks. As more blocks are added, modifying older blocks becomes increasingly challenging.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-computerworld_606253-91)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-econbc-79) In case of disagreement, nodes trust the longest chain, which required the greatest amount of effort to produce.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Mingxiao2017-87) To tamper or censor the ledger, one needs to control the majority of the global [hashrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashrate "Hashrate").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Mingxiao2017-87) The high cost required to reach this level of computational power [secures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_security "Computer security") the bitcoin blockchain.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Mingxiao2017-87)

The [environmental impact of bitcoin mining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_impact_of_bitcoin_mining "Environmental impact of bitcoin mining") is controversial and has attracted the attention of regulators, [leading to restrictions or incentives in various jurisdictions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legality_of_cryptocurrency_by_country_or_territory "Legality of cryptocurrency by country or territory").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Stoll2023-92)As of 2025, a [non-peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-peer-reviewed "Non-peer-reviewed") study by the [Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge_Centre_for_Alternative_Finance "Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance") (CCAF) estimated that bitcoin mining represented 0.5% of [global electricity consumption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_energy_supply_and_consumption "World energy supply and consumption") and 0.08% of world [greenhouse gas emissions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions "Greenhouse gas emissions"), comparable to Slovakia's emissions.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-93) About half of the electricity used is generated through [fossil fuels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossil_fuel "Fossil fuel").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-nytimes_20210903-13) Moreover, mining hardware's short lifespan results in [electronic waste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_waste "Electronic waste").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-deVries2021-94) In October 2025, the US was the largest mining country with 38% of the global bitcoin mining market share, followed by Russia (16%) and China (14%, despite all cryptocurrency trading and mining being banned there in 2021).[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-reuters_20251126-95)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-hashrateindex_20251006-96)

### Privacy and fungibility

Bitcoin is [pseudonymous](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pseudonym "wikt:pseudonym"), with funds linked to addresses, not real-world identities. While the owners of these addresses are not directly identified, all transactions are public on the blockchain. Patterns of use, like spending coins from multiple inputs, can hint at a common owner. Public data can sometimes be matched with known address owners.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-technologyreview_176558-97)[Bitcoin exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_bitcoin_companies "List of bitcoin companies") might also need to collect personal data as per legal requirements.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-washingtonpost_20130821-98) For enhanced [privacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy_and_blockchain "Privacy and blockchain"), users can generate a new address for each transaction.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wired_20130606-99)

In the bitcoin network, each bitcoin is treated equally, ensuring basic [fungibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungibility "Fungibility"). However, users and applications can choose to differentiate between bitcoins. While wallets and software treat all bitcoins the same, each bitcoin's transaction history is recorded on the blockchain. This public record allows for [chain analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain_analysis "Blockchain analysis"), where users can identify and potentially reject bitcoins from controversial sources.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-100) For example, in 2012, Mt. Gox froze accounts containing bitcoins identified as stolen.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-101)

Bitcoin wallets were the first [cryptocurrency wallets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency_wallet "Cryptocurrency wallet"), enabling users to store the information necessary to transact bitcoins.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-motherjones_20130410-102)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 1, glossary The first wallet program, simply named _Bitcoin_, and sometimes referred to as the _Satoshi client_, was released in 2009 by Nakamoto as [open-source software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software "Open-source software").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Humayun-2018-22)[Bitcoin Core](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_Core "Bitcoin Core") is among the best known [clients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Client_(computing) "Client (computing)"). [Forks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fork_(software_development) "Fork (software development)") of Bitcoin Core exist such as [Bitcoin Unlimited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_Unlimited "Bitcoin Unlimited").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wsj_1453044493-103) Wallets can be full clients, with a full copy of the blockchain to check the validity of mined blocks,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 1 or lightweight clients, just to send and receive transactions without a local copy of the entire blockchain.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-104) Third-party internet services, called online wallets or [hot wallets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_wallet "Digital wallet"), store users' credentials on their servers, making them susceptible of hacks.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnbc_20140604-105)[Cold storage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_wallet "Cold wallet") protects bitcoins from such hacks by keeping private keys offline, either through specialized hardware wallets or paper printouts.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-yahoo_140141385-106)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 4

### Scalability and decentralization challenges

Nakamoto limited the block size to one [megabyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megabyte "Megabyte").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-technologyreview_537486-107) The limited block size and frequency can lead to delayed processing of transactions, increased fees and a bitcoin scalability problem.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-technologyreview_537486-107) The [Lightning Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning_Network "Lightning Network"), a [second-layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstraction_layer "Abstraction layer")[routing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Routing "Routing") network, is a potential scaling solution.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Antonopoulos2014-8):ch. 8

Research shows a trend towards centralization in bitcoin as miners join [pools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mining_pool "Mining pool") for stable income.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-JEP-32):215,219–222[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-108):3 If a single miner or pool controls more than 50% of the [hashing power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashrate "Hashrate"), it would allow them to censor transactions and double-spend coins.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Gervais2014-78) In 2014, mining pool [Ghash.io](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghash.io "Ghash.io") reached 51% mining power, causing safety concerns, but later voluntarily capped its power at 39.99% for the benefit of the whole network.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-109) A few entities also dominate other parts of the ecosystem such as the client software, online wallets, and simplified payment verification (SPV) clients.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Gervais2014-78)

## Economics and usage

### Bitcoin's theoretical roots and ideology

According to the [European Central Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Central_Bank "European Central Bank"), the decentralization of money offered by bitcoin has its theoretical roots in the [Austrian school of economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_school_of_economics "Austrian school of economics"), especially with [Friedrich Hayek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Hayek "Friedrich Hayek")'s _[The Denationalisation of Money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Denationalisation\_of\_Money "The Denationalisation of Money")_, in which he advocates a complete [free market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_market "Free market") in the production, distribution and management of money to end the monopoly of [central banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_banks "Central banks").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-europa_201210-110):22 Sociologist [Nigel Dodd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Dodd "Nigel Dodd") argues that the essence of the bitcoin ideology is to remove money from social, as well as governmental, control.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-111)_[The Economist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Economist "The Economist")_ describes bitcoin as "a [techno-anarchist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Techno-anarchist "Techno-anarchist") project to create an online version of cash, a way for people to transact without the possibility of interference from malicious governments or banks".[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-30082018Economist-112) These philosophical ideas initially attracted [libertarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian "Libertarian") and anarchists.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-nytimes_20131214-113)

Money serves three purposes: a [store of value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Store_of_value "Store of value"), a [medium of exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medium_of_exchange "Medium of exchange"), and a [unit of account](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_of_account "Unit of account").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-econ315-114) According to _The Economist_ in 2014, bitcoin functions best as a medium of exchange.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-econ315-114) In 2015, _The Economist_ noted that bitcoins had three qualities useful in a currency: they are "hard to earn, limited in supply and easy to verify".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-economist_21638124-115) However, a 2018 assessment by _The Economist_ stated that cryptocurrencies met none of these three criteria.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-30082018Economist-112) Per some researchers, as of 2015, bitcoin functions more as a [payment system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payment_system "Payment system") than as a currency.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-JEP-32) In 2014, economist [Robert J. Shiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_J._Shiller "Robert J. Shiller") wrote that bitcoin has potential as a unit of account for measuring the relative value of goods, as with Chile's [Unidad de Fomento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unidad_de_Fomento "Unidad de Fomento"), but that "Bitcoin in its present form... doesn't really solve any sensible economic problem".[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Shiller-116) In 2017, François Velde, senior economist at the [Chicago Fed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Fed "Chicago Fed"), described bitcoin as "unlikely by itself to replace monies in well-functioning monetary systems."[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-117)

The [legal status of bitcoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legality_of_cryptocurrency_by_country_or_territory "Legality of cryptocurrency by country or territory") varies substantially from one jurisdiction to another. Because of its decentralized nature and its global presence, regulating bitcoin is difficult. However, the use of bitcoin can be criminalized, and shutting down exchanges and the peer-to-peer economy in a given country would constitute a de facto ban.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-pastemagazine_20170918-118) The [use of bitcoin by criminals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency_and_crime "Cryptocurrency and crime") has attracted the attention of financial regulators, legislative bodies, and law enforcement.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloombergview_20130808-119) Nobel-prize winning economist [Joseph Stiglitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stiglitz "Joseph Stiglitz") says that bitcoin's anonymity encourages [money laundering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_laundering "Money laundering") and other crimes.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnbc_20180709-120) This is the main justification behind bitcoin bans.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-SunYin2019-12)As of November 2021, nine countries applied an absolute ban (Algeria, Bangladesh, China, Egypt, Iraq, Morocco, Nepal, Qatar, and Tunisia) while another 42 countries had an implicit ban.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-LOC2021-121)[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_]

to [freelancers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freelancer "Freelancer").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloomberg_20180801-126)As of 2015, there was little sign of bitcoin use in international [remittances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remittance "Remittance") despite high fees charged by banks and [Western Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Union "Western Union").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-JEP-32)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-scmp_1679904-127)

From September 2021 until January 2025, the [Bitcoin Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_Law "Bitcoin Law") made bitcoin a [legal tender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_tender "Legal tender") currency in El Salvador, alongside the US dollar.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-BTCSVSept7FT-9) The adoption had been criticized internationally and within El Salvador.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-BTCSVSept7FT-9)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-reuters_20210902-128) In 2022, the [International Monetary Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund") (IMF) urged El Salvador to reverse its decision.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bbc_60135552-129)As of 2022, the use of [Bitcoin in El Salvador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_in_El_Salvador "Bitcoin in El Salvador") remained low: 80% of businesses refused to accept it.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-130) In 2025, El Salvador's government revoked bitcoin's status as legal tender currency to comply with conditions set by the IMF for a loan. El Salvador still describes bitcoin as "legal tender", but its acceptance is no longer obligitory (as it is with the US dollar) and the El Salvador government no longer accepts bitcoin for payment of taxes or fees.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-El_Salvador_Abandons_Bitcoin_as_Legal_Tender-10)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Bitcoin_is_no_longer_legal_tender_in_El_Salvador-11)

In April 2022, the Central African Republic (CAR) adopted bitcoin as legal tender alongside the [CFA franc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CFA_franc "CFA franc"),[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloomberg_20220428-131) but repealed the reform one year later.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-132)

Bitcoin is also used by some governments. For instance, the [Iranian government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Iran "Government of Iran") initially opposed cryptocurrencies, but later began using them to circumvent [sanctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanctions_against_Iran "Sanctions against Iran").[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-vice_20201103-133) Since 2020, Iran has required local bitcoin miners to sell bitcoin to the [Central Bank of Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Iran "Central Bank of Iran"), allowing the central bank to use it for imports.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-aawsat202011-134) Some [constituent states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constituent_state "Constituent state") and local governments also accept tax payments in bitcoin, including [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") in the US[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-denverpost_20220921-135) and [Zug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton_of_Zug "Canton of Zug") and [Lugano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lugano "Lugano") in Switzerland.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-swissinfo_46010364-136)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-swissinfo_49032696-137) As of 2023, the US government owned more than $5 billion worth of seized bitcoin.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wsj_20231015-138)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-forbes_20230616-139)

### Use for investment and status as an economic bubble

[![Image 13](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/El_Salvador_Bitcoin_reserves.png/250px-El_Salvador_Bitcoin_reserves.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:El_Salvador_Bitcoin_reserves.png)

Government website with El Salvador reserves

As of 2018, the overwhelming majority of bitcoin transactions took place on [cryptocurrency exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency_exchange "Cryptocurrency exchange").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-FT08062018-124) Since 2014, regulated bitcoin funds also allow [exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_exposure "Market exposure") to the asset or to [futures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Futures_contract "Futures contract") as an investment.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bbc_28247796-140)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cbsnews_20171218-141) Bitcoin is used as a [store of value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Store_of_value "Store of value"):[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloomberg_20211025-142)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-reuters_20220105-143) individuals and companies such as the [Winklevoss twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winklevoss_Capital_Management "Winklevoss Capital Management")[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-144) and [Elon Musk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk "Elon Musk")'s companies [SpaceX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX "SpaceX") and [Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc.") have each bought and sold hundreds of millions of dollars worth of bitcoin.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-145)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wsj_20230817-146)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wsj_11612791688-147) Bitcoin wealth is highly concentrated, with 0.01% holding 27% of in-circulation currency, as of 2021.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-wsj_11639996204-148)

As of March 2025, El Salvador had $550 million worth of bitcoin in its [international reserves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_exchange_reserves "Foreign exchange reserves"), about 6,102 coins.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-reuters_20250305-149)

Bitcoin, along with other cryptocurrencies, has been described as an [economic bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_bubble "Economic bubble") by several economists, including [Nobel Prize in Economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") laureates, such as [Joseph Stiglitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stiglitz "Joseph Stiglitz"),[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Stiglitz-150)[James Heckman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Heckman "James Heckman"),[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-4Nobels-151) and [Paul Krugman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Krugman "Paul Krugman").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-Krugman-152) Another recipient of the prize, [Robert Shiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Shiller "Robert Shiller"), argues that bitcoin is rather a [fad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fad "Fad") that may become an [asset class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asset_classes "Asset classes"). He describes its price growth as an "epidemic", driven by [contagious narratives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_contagion "Social contagion").[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloomberg_20210609-153) In 2024, [Jean Tirole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Tirole "Jean Tirole"), also Nobel laureate, described bitcoin as a "pure bubble" as its [intrinsic value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrinsic_value_(finance) "Intrinsic value (finance)") is zero. According to him, some bubbles are long-lasting such as gold and fiat currencies, and it is impossible to predict whether bitcoin would implode like other financial bubbles or become an alternative to gold.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-154) The same year, [Federal Reserve Chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chair_of_the_Federal_Reserve "Chair of the Federal Reserve")[Jerome Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerome_Powell "Jerome Powell") described bitcoin as a digital competitor to gold but not to the dollar as he argued it is a highly volatile [speculative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speculation "Speculation") asset not used as a form of payment.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-155) In 2025, [Kenneth Rogoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Rogoff "Kenneth Rogoff") claimed that Krugman was wrong and that Bitcoin had value as it is competing with the dollar to become the [means of exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Means_of_exchange "Means of exchange") of the [underground economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Informal_economy "Informal economy") which represents 20% of the world's GDP.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-RogoffEconomist-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-RogoffBloomberg-123) According to Rogoff, bitcoin is "the ideal currency for a more fragmented and uncertain global landscape" and it could become appealing to [emerging-market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emerging_market "Emerging market") central banks as a "politically neutral" [reserve currency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_currency "Reserve currency").[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-:0-156) In 2025, the nominee for the Chair of the Federal Reserve, [Kevin Warsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Warsh "Kevin Warsh"), described Bitcoin as the "new gold."[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-:0-156)

According to research published in the _[International Review of Financial Analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International\_Review\_of\_Financial\_Analysis "International Review of Financial Analysis")_ in 2018, bitcoin as an asset is highly volatile and does not behave like any other conventional asset.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-qub_155247201-157) According to one 2022 analysis published in _[The Journal of Alternative Investments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Journal\_of\_Alternative\_Investments "The Journal of Alternative Investments")_, bitcoin was less volatile than [oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Price_of_oil "Price of oil"), [silver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_as_an_investment "Silver as an investment"), [US Treasuries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Treasury_security "United States Treasury security"), and 190 stocks in the [S&P 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S&P_500 "S&P 500") during and after the [2020 stock market crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_stock_market_crash "2020 stock market crash").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-158) The term _[hodl](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/hodl#English "wikt:hodl")_ was created in December 2013 for [holding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buy_and_hold "Buy and hold") bitcoin rather than selling it during periods of volatility.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnbc_20180826-159)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-bloomberg_20201119-160)

In 2014, economist [Nouriel Roubini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nouriel_Roubini "Nouriel Roubini") described bitcoin as a [Ponzi scheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponzi_scheme "Ponzi scheme").[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-cnbc_20140310-161) Legal scholar [Eric Posner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Posner "Eric Posner") disagrees, however, as "a real Ponzi scheme takes fraud; bitcoin, by contrast, seems more like a collective [delusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delusion "Delusion")".[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-slate_20130411-162) A 2014 [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank") report also concluded that bitcoin was not a deliberate Ponzi scheme.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-163)

### Market characteristics

Bitcoin markets operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, contrasting with traditional financial markets that have fixed trading hours. Bitcoin prices show much higher volatility and respond strongly to both regulatory changes and market events.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-164)

The volume of bitcoin trading can fluctuate considerably among various exchanges and geographic regions. The daily transaction volume of bitcoin across all exchanges typically reaches $50 billion as of 2025.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin#cite_note-indiatimes_120988931-165)
